name: BOB Gear Revolution Flex 3.0
price_note: BOB Gear US list price (single jogger)

specs.child_range: Birth with infant car seat (walk only); seat from 8 wk (walk only); jog/off-road from 8 mo; up to 75 lb / 44 in; 5-point no-rethread harness
specs.fold: 38 x 25 x 16 in (wheels on); BGL measured 14,748 cu in

recall_status: None found 2016-2026 for this model. BOB brand: 17-088 (2017, BOB Motion Click & Go receivers), 19-763 (2019, campaign thru-bolt axles); 2018 CPSC lawsuit settled without recall (older quick-release joggers).
investigation: BOB brand history: CPSC sued Britax in Feb 2018 over pre-Sept-2015 BOB quick-release front wheels (about 200 detachment reports, 97 injuries alleged); settled Nov 2018 (3-2 vote) as an information campaign, no recall; ~200 replacement thru-bolt axles were then recalled in 2019 (19-763). Current models are not part of that dispute.
why: Ranked on evidence (lab tests first, then recalls, then proven features, then usability): highest BabyGearLab score (77, #3 of 10, 'Best for long-term use') of the joggers with a clean current-model record and no running warning; has a handlebar wrist strap and 5-point harness. Wirecutter is lukewarm (fine if you avoid rough terrain) and it lacks a hand brake, so it is not an unqualified win.
cautions: No hand (deceleration) brake - BabyGearLab and BOB spec
Two-hand fold, does not self-stand
Walk only until 8 months; no jogging before 8 months (BOB)
Buying used: pre-Sept-2015 BOB quick-release joggers were the subject of the 2018 CPSC lawsuit and were never formally recalled
sources: BOB Gear product page (specs, wrist strap)
CPSC: CPSC and Britax settle BOB lawsuit

name: BOB Gear Alterrain Pro
price_note: BOB Gear US list price; BabyGearLab listed $780-830

specs.child_range: Infant car seat 0-8 wk (walk only); seat from 8 wk (walk only); jog/off-road from 8 mo; up to 75 lb / 44 in; 5-point no-rethread harness
specs.fold: 39.3 x 25.5 x 16 in (wheels on); BGL measured 17,357 cu in

recall_status: None found 2016-2026 for this model. BOB brand: 17-088 (2017), 19-763 (2019); 2018 CPSC lawsuit settled without recall (older quick-release joggers).
investigation: BOB brand history: CPSC sued Britax in Feb 2018 over pre-Sept-2015 BOB quick-release front wheels (about 200 detachment reports, 97 injuries alleged); settled Nov 2018 (3-2 vote) as an information campaign, no recall; ~200 replacement thru-bolt axles were then recalled in 2019 (19-763). Current models are not part of that dispute.
why: Ranked on evidence: BabyGearLab score 74 (#5 of 10) is close to the Revolution Flex, and it adds the safety features the Flex lacks - a hand brake plus handlebar wrist strap and 5-point harness; Wirecutter names it the BOB to get if you want a hand brake. Slightly lower lab score keeps it at #2.

Heavy (31-33 lb) and long; poor indoors
No jogging before 8 months (BOB)
BabyGearLab 2020 combo test called the 3-part car seat adapter 'wobbly'
sources: CPSC: CPSC and Britax settle BOB lawsuit

name: Guava Roam Crossover (Roam Stroller)

specs.child_range: From 6 months in seat (birth with car seat adapter, sold separately); up to 60 lb
specs.fold: 29 x 15 x 17 in (Guava); BGL measured 7,488 cu in

recall_status: Recalled: CPSC 25-032 (2024-11-07), about 8,500 Roam strollers - brakes can fail to engage or can disengage (67 + 152 reports, no injuries); free repair kit.
why: Best independent test result in the group (BabyGearLab 88, #1 'Best Overall'; Wirecutter lists it as a compact option), but a 2024 CPSC brake recall drops it below the clean-record BOB models under the evidence rule.
cautions: Check that recalled units have the brake repair kit fitted (CPSC 25-032)
No hand (deceleration) brake
Max 60 lb, lower than BOB's 75 lb
Wirecutter: bumpier ride from airless tires

name: BOB Gear Wayfinder

specs.child_range: Infant car seat only until head/neck control; child up to 65 lb / 44 in (75 lb total capacity incl. basket); 5-point harness

recall_status: None found 2016-2026 for this model. BOB brand history as for other BOB models.
investigation: BOB brand history: CPSC sued Britax in Feb 2018 over pre-Sept-2015 BOB quick-release front wheels (about 200 detachment reports, 97 injuries alleged); settled Nov 2018 (3-2 vote) as an information campaign, no recall; ~200 replacement thru-bolt axles were then recalled in 2019 (19-763). Current models are not part of that dispute.
why: Wirecutter's rough-terrain pick (Feb 2026) with a bicycle-style hand brake, handlebar wrist strap and 5-point harness, and no recalls; ranked below the BOB models with two-lab coverage because only one independent tester has evaluated it.
cautions: Only one independent test (Wirecutter); not in BabyGearLab's lineup
Max child weight 65 lb per BOB spec (marketing cites 75 lb total)
BOB: do not jog in swivel mode or with a child lacking head/neck control
sources: CPSC: CPSC and Britax settle BOB lawsuit

name: Chicco Activ3 Jogging Stroller

specs.child_range: Up to 50 lb; works with all Chicco infant car seats via included tray/adapter

recall_status: None found 2016-2026 for this model (Chicco's only entry in the recall set is a 2025 MyFit car-seat campaign).
why: Wirecutter's budget pick (adjustable suspension, ~half the price of the BOBs) with a wrist strap/jogging tether in the box and a clean recall record; one-lab evidence and no hand brake keep it mid-list.

Lower 50 lb limit and smaller basket than picks above
Only one independent test; BabyGearLab did not test it
sources: Chicco product page (50 lb, wrist strap/tether)

name: Baby Jogger Summit X3
price_note: Baby Jogger US list price; on sale for $439.99 on 2026-10-04

specs.child_range: Birth (with car seat, adapters sold separately) up to 75 lb / 44 in; consult pediatrician before jogging under 6 months; 5-point harness (rethread straps)
specs.fold: BGL measured 34.5 x 25.8 x 15 in (13,326 cu in)

recall_status: None found 2016-2026 (no Baby Jogger recalls in the CPSC/NHTSA set).
why: Strong safety kit (hand deceleration brake, handlebar tether strap, all-wheel suspension) and a clean recall record, but both labs rate it weakly: BabyGearLab 61 (#7 of 10; its brake 'not as effective as other handbrakes') and Wirecutter found it hard to push - so it ranks last of the joggers.
cautions: BabyGearLab: deceleration brake weaker than rivals; harness hard to adjust
Wirecutter: difficult to push, not worth the price
10 lb basket limit; overloading can make it unstable (manual)
sources: Baby Jogger product page (brake, tether, 75 lb)

name: Veer All-Terrain Cruiser
price_note: Veer US price; Cruiser XL is $799

specs.child_range: 2 seats, 55 lb per seat; 6+ months in seat, 0-6 mo with infant car seat adapter (sold separately); 3-point harnesses (5-point via Comfort Seat accessory)
specs.fold: 37 x 20 x 14 in (Wirecutter); 37 x 20 x 9 in wheels off

recall_status: None found 2016-2026 (CPSC API returned no Veer recalls).
why: Wagon group #1. Top-scored wagon in Kid Travel's 13-wagon lab test (83, Editor's Choice; best build quality, folding and steering) and Wirecutter's 'Also great' outdoor pick; no recalls. Note there is no stand-alone US wagon standard yet (ASTM WK94774 is adding wagons to F833).
cautions: Only 3-point harnesses as standard; CR strongly recommends 5-point
Low wagon walls - kids can reach wheels when pulled (Wirecutter)
Canopy, basket and car seat adapter cost extra
'Meets ASTM/JPMA' is a maker claim; no wagon-specific standard is final
sources: CR stroller wagons (no mandatory wagon standard)

name: Baby Trend Expedition 2-in-1 Stroller Wagon Plus
price_note: Baby Trend regular price; on sale for $239.99 on 2026-10-04

specs.child_range: 2 seats, 55 lb per seat (110 lb total); 6+ months (sits unassisted); 0-6 mo with included infant car seat adapter; 3-point harness

recall_status: None found 2016-2026 for this wagon. Brand: Baby Trend Cityscape jogger 22-772 (2022, parking brake) and Tango Mini 20-052 (2020), plus car-seat campaigns.
why: Wagon group #2. Wirecutter's top stroller-wagon pick (Mar 2026) and a 76 in Kid Travel's lab test (tested as 'Baby Trend Expedition' wagon), with a one-step brake and included car seat adapter at the lowest price here; 3-point harnesses keep it below the Veer.
cautions: 3-point harnesses only - Wirecutter warns small toddlers can slip out; CR recommends 5-point
Heavy (about 40 lb) and not compact folded
Canopy does not fully cover two kids (Wirecutter)

name: Larktale caravan coupe V2

specs.child_range: 2 seats, 6 months up to 65 lb per seat (152 lb total); newborn via car seat adapters for Maxi-Cosi, Nuna, Clek; no-rethread harness (point count not confirmed)

recall_status: None found 2016-2026 (CPSC API returned no Larktale recalls).
why: Wagon group #3. Earlier Larktale models tested well - the full-size Caravan scored 80 (Recommended) at Kid Travel and Wirecutter liked an earlier Coupe's very high walls, reclining seats and smooth ride - and there are no recalls; the current V2 itself has not been lab-tested, so evidence is Limited.
cautions: Independent tests were on earlier/larger versions, not this exact V2
Harness type (3- vs 5-point) not confirmed from the maker page
Bulky canopies; snack tray extra (Wirecutter)
Heavy (about 40 lb)

name: Evenflo Pivot Xplore All-Terrain Stroller Wagon
price_note: Evenflo US price; Adventurer Gray showed sold out on 2026-10-04

specs.child_range: 2 seats, 6 months+ up to 55 lb per child (110 lb total); infant car seat adapter for Evenflo seats sold separately

recall_status: None found 2016-2026 for this wagon (Evenflo's recalls in the set are car-seat/travel-system campaigns).
why: Wagon group #4. Two labs disagree: Kid Travel scored it 80 (Recommended; handles like a stroller, folds small) but Wirecutter dropped it because it listed to one side with two kids and its rear wheels lock separately - Kid Travel also rated its braking weakest-tier (5/10).
cautions: Two separate rear brakes - easy to leave one unlocked; slower stops (Kid Travel)
Tips over when standing folded (storage hazard)
Wirecutter: lists to one side when loaded; kids outgrow it sooner
Harness type not confirmed
